newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS DOWNED BY RUSEDSKI SERVING BLITZ.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS DOWNED BY RUSEDSKI SERVING BLITZ.

text.p: Britain's Greg Rusedski won Wimbledon's first-round serving duel on Tuesday, blitzing lofty seventh-seeded Australian Mark Philippoussis 7-6 7-6 6-3.

The battle between the two fastest recorded servers in tennis took just 14 minutes to complete after the pair had suspended play in the gathering gloom of Monday night with Rusedski, 3-1 up in the third set.

The win compensated the partisan crowd for the embarrassing disappointment of the day's first match on the Centre Court where Britain's Clare Wood succumbed 6-0 6-0 to a rampant Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, runner up here for the last two years.

Rusedski, ranked 27 in the world, carried on where he left off, adding six aces to his overnight tally for a total of 27 in the match. He kept his nerve and, though Philippoussis saved two match points in the eighth game of the set, refused to give the 20-year-old from Melbourne a chance to square the set.
"It opens up the draw for me now," he said. "I just want to keep on the roll and keep on winning. The crowd really helped me out," he said.

Despite a couple of sweet returns, Philippoussis could not keep his game consistent. Rusedski, whose fastest recorded serve timed at 225 kph is second only to Philippoussis's 229 kph, finished the match with an ace.

Philippoussis, who showed better form on grass at Queen's where he beat Goran Ivanisevic in the final, managed only 14 aces and nearly matched them with 13 double faults compared with Rusedski's three.
"Greg wasn't exactly an ideal first round draw, especially in a Grand Slam," Philippoussis said. "If he goes on serving like that in his other matches, who knows how far he can go."
French Open Champion Gustavo Kuerten was the second seed to bite the lush Wimbledon turf, going down after a lusty fight back against Justin Gimelstob 6-3 6-4 4-6 1-6 6-4.

The 19-year-old Brazilian 11th seed, who shot up the rankings to 12th after his Paris triumph, was playing only his second match on grass and was beaten by the 117th-ranked Gimelstob's more expert serve and volley game.
Sanchez Vicario showed scant sympathy for her British victim. "I did not want to spend too long on court," she said.
The 25-year-old is seeded only eighth this year after mixed fortunes on the circuit, but she looked comfortable on grass after reaching the rain-abandoned final at Eastbourne last Sunday.

Women's top seed Martina Hingis, runner-up at the French Open, by contrast,looked distinctly ill-at-ease against Luxembourg amateur qualifier Anne Kremer, ranked 218 in the world. The 16-year-old, who won her first Grand Slam tournament in Australia this year needed six match points to finish Kremer, who chased every ball, 6-4 6-4.

The 1994 champion Conchita Martinez, seeded 10, beat Karina Habsudova of Slovakia 6-1 6-2 in under an hour but men's 15th seed Wayne Ferreira needed two hours and 47 minutes to beat Australia's Scott Draper 6-7 3-6 6-4 6-0 7-5 in a match held over from Monday.
Three-times former champion Boris Becker survived his first round on court two, known as the graveyard of the seeds, beating Marcos Aurelio Gorriz of Spain 6-3 6-2 6-3.
Last year Becker, who calls Wimbledon his back garden, was bitterly disappointed when he had to retire injured after rupturing a tendon in his first round match.
Brenda Schultz-McCarthy, who beat Monica Seles on grass in Eastbourne last week, came back from a set down to beat Italian Silvia Farina 4-6 6-3 6-2 .
Schultz-McCarthy, the 14th seed, is the biggest server in the women's game but while her serve was powerful on Tuesday it was not always accurate.

But after a wobbly first set Farina, who at one point resorted to serving underarm, was broken twice in the deciding set to put Schultz-McCarthy 4-1 up. The Dutchwoman saved a breakpoint in the eighth game before serving out for victory.

But Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman, the 17 seed who beat world number one Pete Sampras at Queen's earlier this month, could not keep his grass court form going and went down in five sets to Britain's Chris Wilkinson.
